transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-07
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Price (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Liam Ortega (HelioOps), Sara Kim (HelioOps), Anna Voss (HelioOps)

Summary (auto): Quick hands-on demo of JSON mode + typed invocations, showing deterministic outputs + schema validation, plus Console Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization. Talked about privacy (KMS/audit logs) and pilot next steps.

00:00 Ethan: okay everyone thanks for joining, i'm ethan from redwood inference, happy to do a short workshop/demo focused on typed invocations and how you might wire it into helioops' alert summarization pipeline
00:17 Liam: hey thanks ethan, excited to see how we can get predictable json outputs — our summaries need structured fields for severity, root_cause, and actions, otherwise downstream automation breaks
00:30 Priya: cool, i'll jump in with the API examples — we'll show console first for visibility then the api flow and a tiny benchmark in optimize. bear with me if typing is slow, uh — my wifi is meh today
00:46 Anna: quick ask up front — we run in a VPC and have strict egress. is this demo going to show anything about private deploy or just hosted?
00:58 Ethan: good question — today's is hosted demo + sandbox, but we will cover private and dedicated options and what changes (networking, kms, audit logs) during the security section
01:12 Priya: alright i'm sharing my screen — first slide is the JSON mode quickstart: you define a schema, attach it to a model route, and the runtime will enforce/validate and optionally return a structured error with reasons (e.g., missing required field)
01:30 Priya: here's a sample schema we used for alerts: {"type":"object","properties":{"severity":{"type":"string"},"root_cause":{"type":"string"},"actions":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}},"required":["severity","root_cause"]} — ok that might get mangled in the transcript, but file link is in the notes
01:52 Liam: that looks good — how strict is validation? if model returns slightly different tokenization like 'high-priority' vs 'high' will it fail?
02:04 Priya: by default we provide a tolerant mode: we do schema coercion attempts and structured fallbacks. you can set mode=strict if you want automatic rejection on mismatch. for your pipeline i'd recommend tolerant+scoring so you still get payloads but with a validation flag
02:23 Sara: is the coercion done client-side or at runtime? does that affect latency?
02:30 Priya: it's runtime — small CPU step, usually sub 10ms for typical payload sizes. latency impact depends on sequence length but it's negligible compared to token generation. in Optimize we also profile this and suggest config changes
02:47 Ethan: jumping in — one of the reasons teams pick Redwood is the combined routing + fallback story: if the primed model variant doesn't satisfy cost or latency you can fallback to a cheaper quantized variant or to a shorter context route without changing schemas
03:02 Anna: can we see a live invocation?
03:06 Priya: yes i'll call the api from the console playground — sending a sample alert now — payload includes last_5_logs and topology metadata.
03:16 [0:03:16] Priya: POST /v1/generate -> model: aurora-xl-rls, mode: json
03:28 [0:03:28] System: stream begins -> { partial: {"severity":"high","root_cause":"disk_io_spike"} 
03:42 Liam: nice, streaming structured partials — that helps the consumer microservice act earlier
03:51 Priya: completed: {"severity":"high","root_cause":"disk_io_spike","actions":["scale-io-nodes","restart-daemon"]} validation: passed
04:08 Sara: does the runtime attach provenance or a validation score to the response? we need to show auditors why a certain action was suggested
04:17 Priya: yes, the response metadata has a validation_score and a model_confidence float. it's in the response envelope and available in console logs and tracing. we also keep token-level cost and latency breakdowns in the Console traces
04:33 Liam: videocall comment: any SOC2/ISO support? we will need audit logs retained 1 year for some customers
04:43 Ethan: we support SOC 2 type II as a company; for Private/Dedicated deployments you can configure audit log retention and push logs to your SIEM. we also integrate with KMS for customer-managed keys on Private
04:56 Anna: what's the KMS integration look like? bring-your-own-key?
05:02 Priya: yes BYOK is supported on private; hosted customers can use envelope encryption with our KMS, and enterprise can request HSM integrations. we'll share the security pack in the follow-up
05:15 [0:05:15] Priya: next i'm going to demo function/tool calling — the idea is you keep model output typed and then map fields to downstream tool calls safely. example: if actions contains 'scale-io-nodes' we'll generate a typed call that the orchestrator can accept
05:31 Priya: invoking tool: scale_cluster({"cluster_id":"c-123","units":2}) -> success
05:43 Liam: do we have guardrails to prevent dangerous actions like 'delete-db'? how are those enforced?
05:51 Priya: yes there are multilayer guardrails: schema allowlists, runtime action whitelists, and a policy layer where you can set human-in-the-loop for high-risk actions. you can also mark certain tool calls as non-autonomous and require explicit approval in Console
06:10 Sara: from a network perspective if we go private, can the tool invocations happen entirely inside our VPC?
06:18 Ethan: yes for private deployments the runtime can be deployed in your VPC so calls never egress to public internet; in dedicated there are configs for service endpoints and peering
06:28 Anna: how about RBAC and SSO? we use SAML for SSO and need per-route RBAC for who can enable auto-execution of actions
06:37 Priya: Console supports SAML/SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and RBAC at token and route level — you can require specific roles to flip the 'auto-execute' flag on a model route
06:50 [0:06:50] Priya: switching over to Optimize — i'll show the suggestions engine. we ran a small profiling job earlier against your sample traces and Optimize suggested batching=16 for steady-state and quantization profile int8 for aurora-medium to cut latency/cost
07:06 Priya: here's the recommendations sheet -> estimated token cost down 38% and p99 latency from 420ms to ~210ms with caching + batching. link: https://console.redwood.ai/optimize/recs/HE-0173
07:22 Liam: neat. what's the tradeoff on quality? we've got strict accuracy thresholds for root_cause detection
07:29 Priya: Optimize gives expected quality delta per suggestion. for the int8 quantization the expected drop on root_cause F1 is ~1.2% based on our eval set. we also recommend running canary rollouts with A/B using the rollout feature
07:42 Ethan: you can set automatic fallback if quality drops below threshold — runtime will route to full-precision model for those queries and log the event
07:53 Anna: let's talk pilot scope — what's a minimal pilot you recommend to validate this?
07:59 Priya: minimal pilot: 2-week sandbox with a subset of alerts (1000/day), run against hosted sandbox route to validate schemas, then 1-week benchmark with dedicated routing and Optimize suggestions enabled. we'll measure p99 latency, token cost per processed alert, and root_cause F1
08:18 Liam: that sounds reasonable. one more question: for long contexts (we include 5-10 pages of logs sometimes) how does KV cache and batching behave?
08:29 Priya: KV cache helps when you have repeated prefixes/metadata; batching is per-request shape — Optimize will show you request size distribution and suggest batching or truncation policies. for huge contexts we recommend prefix cache + chunking before sending to model to avoid blowing up token costs
08:49 Sara: are there any hard limits on attachment size on hosted? we have regulatory attachments sometimes
08:55 Ethan: hosted has soft limits and can be tuned for dedicated/private placements. for regulated attachments we'd advise private with dedicated nodes and bring-your-own-key for encryption
09:06 [0:09:06] Priya: i'm going to run a small scripted benchmark now — sending 50 synthetic alerts through the sandbox route with varied lengths
09:22 [0:09:22] System: benchmark run started -> avg latency 230ms, p99 480ms with current toy config
09:33 Liam: that's promising. what about cost math? can you show the per-alert token breakdown?
09:40 Priya: yes, Console shows token counts per stage: prompt tokens, context tokens, generation tokens. here's a breakdown exported to CSV in the shared folder
09:51 Anna: could you also include the Optimize recommendation that would get us to the 200ms p99 target we mentioned earlier?
09:57 Priya: noted — i'll include a focused optimize run and a config diff in the follow-up
10:04 [0:10:04] Ethan: switching gears — procurement/security questions: does Redwood do contract E-Discovery or allow specific data deletion on request?
10:13 Priya: yes, for enterprise and private we have controls to delete customer data and retention policies; we'll send the compliance pack including DPA and deletion flows
10:23 Liam: are there any known integration partners for our observability stack (we use Splunk and Datadog)?
10:31 Ethan: yes both Splunk and Datadog integrations exist; we can export traces and metrics to your endpoints and push audit logs as well
10:39 Sara: are there any gotchas when running in an air-gapped environment?
10:45 Priya: air-gapped is possible but needs an on-prem package and a bit more setup for model updates; it also means you'll handle your own KMS/HSM and patching cadence. we'll detail the installer steps in the private playbook
10:58 [0:10:58] Priya: quick demo of a guarded tool flow — model outputs action 'restart-daemon' but the policy denies automatic execution because that action is in the high-risk list; instead a task is created in Console with one-click approve
11:18 Anna: that approval flow is ideal — product team can review before auto-actions are allowed
11:25 Liam: any metrics on false positives for root cause? curious how often the model hallucinated an action in your beta runs
11:33 Priya: in our internal evals the hallucination rate for explicit action strings was <4% after prompt engineering and schema constraints; Optimize also surfaces prompt sensitivity experiments to reduce that further
11:48 Ethan: ok wrapping up — let's recap next steps and owners
11:54 Ethan: action list: ethan send SOW + pricing, priya send sandbox configs + schema + focused optimize run, helioops to send anonymized logs and confirm success metrics, sara to confirm networking and KMS details
12:09 Anna: sounds good. i think we can start the pilot next week if the paperwork is quick
12:16 Liam: i'll coordinate internally and aim to have logs and criteria by the 14th
12:22 Ethan: great; i'll follow up with calendar invites and links to the shared folder. thanks everyone!
12:30 [End transcript — 52 minutes total]
